findings.evidence: scripts/task-run-guard.py:315-346 computes a global monotonic deadline before validation and journal work, but then unconditionally calls Popen after writing the attempt. If pin validation, lock/accounting, or journal I/O consumes the remaining budget, the command still starts; max(0.001, remaining) only bounds the subsequent wait. The action can therefore perform side effects after the session deadline.
findings.property: The approved command must not be launched after the original session deadline, and command duration must fit the remaining budget.
findings.falsifier: Show that every execution rechecks the remaining monotonic budget immediately before spawn and refuses without launching when it is exhausted; include a regression that delays validation or journal accounting until past the deadline and asserts the child marker is absent.

findings.evidence: scripts/task-run-guard.py:273-278 uses one os.write(data) and ignores the returned byte count. A short write can leave a partial identity/attempt/result record while append_record returns normally. In the attempt case, run then proceeds to Popen despite not having durably recorded the complete pre-spawn attempt, undermining persistent attempt accounting.
findings.property: Every launch must have a complete, durable attempt record written before spawn; accounting failures must refuse launch.
findings.falsifier: Demonstrate a write-all loop or equivalent full-length check that refuses before spawn on incomplete journal writes, with a focused regression simulating a short write and asserting the command marker remains absent.
